newsitem.title: USA: CME traders call USDA data bearish for CME cattle.
newsitem.headline: CME traders call USDA data bearish for CME cattle.

text.p: Chicago Mercantile Exchange cattle traders expect CME live cattle futures to open 0.50 cent per lb lower in the April contract Tuesday and 1.00 cent lower in June and August because of Friday's bearishly-construed U.S. Agriculture Department Cattle on Feed report.
CME feeder cattle were expected to open at least 0.50 cent lower Tuesday.
CME futures markets will be closed Monday in observance of the U.S. Presidents Day holiday.

The most bearish aspect of the report were the surprisingly large January placements, which USDA reported at 125 percent of a year ago, traders noted. That was about 10 percentage points greater than the largest estimate in a Reuter pre-report survey. The pre-report estimates ranged from 99.0 to 114.6 percent of a year ago.
"With grain prices about half of what they were a year ago...you would obviously think that would tend to push placements higher," said Dan Vaught, livestock analyst with A.G.Edwards & Sons Inc.

Vaught said analysts may have underestimated the placement activity because the large number of feeder cattle auctions throughout the country make it difficult to accurately assess movement into feedlots.

At 107 percent of a year ago, the report's January marketings figure for the seven primary cattle feeding states was seen as bullish for April live cattle, but analysts and traders expect April to open about 0.50 cent lower, pulled down by the bearish placement figure.
